output.summary: KEP-554 proposed per-node dynamic volume attach limits, tracked in the CSINode object, and a single scheduler predicate covering both in-tree and CSI volumes. The KEP's status is implemented at stable stage, per the given fact; the feature graduated to GA in 1.17.
output.rationale: The existing limits came from cluster-wide defaults on Node objects, and CSI limits used prefixed, SHA-hashed resource names that were not user-readable. The proposal moves limits to CSINode and lets in-tree and CSI drivers share one limit. Discussion shows the feature stayed in beta through 1.13-1.16 and was announced as GA for 1.17, after which the KEP was updated to implemented. The sources do not explain the later 2021 PR dispute over status labels in detail.

alternatives.option: Keep cluster-global defaults and in-tree-only hard-coded predicates (MaxEBSVolumeCount, MaxGCEPDVolumeCount, etc.)
alternatives.why_not: The design doc says it is 'problematic for CSI' and that the resource names cannot be made readable, and it prevents in-tree and CSI drivers from sharing a limit.

alternatives.option: Proposal #730 (CSI volume limits via node resource names)
alternatives.why_not: The readme says this proposal 'replaces #730' and integrates in-tree and CSI volumes into one predicate.

evidence.quote: This proposal replaces [#730](https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/pull/730) and integrates volume limits for in-tree volumes
